name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd

ledger.quote: Ahead of the festive season we expect volume growth of at least 15% quarter-on-quarter.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.target: Volume growth of at least 15% QoQ
ledger.verdict: Q2 FY26 quarterly volume growth was not specified in reported financial results.

ledger.quote: Construction of our 0.8 million square feet. mobile manufacturing campus is progressing well in Noida for our anchor customers with much higher capacity and is expected to be completed by March ‘26.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.verdict: Could not verify the evidence for this one in the latest call.

ledger.quote: Tentative agreements pertaining to the transaction are expected to be closed in another couple of months, and we expect the financials to start consolidating from Q3 of the current financial year.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.target: Consolidate Q Tech financials from Q3
ledger.verdict: Q Tech financials were consolidated into Dixon as a subsidiary.
ledger.evidence: We are expanding the capacities of camera module in subsidiary Q Tech, which is an ECMS beneficiary for smartphones from 70 million annually to 180 million to 190 million annually

ledger.quote: Construction of our facility for display modules in which we have a 74:26 JV with HKC for first phase underway for smartphones and notebooks with trials to be commenced from Q4 this fiscal and commencement of mass production by Q1 of next fiscal.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.target: Mass production by Q1 next fiscal
ledger.verdict: Mass production for display JV targeted for Q1 FY27 was delayed to late Q3 or Q4 FY27.
ledger.evidence: Construction of our display facility is completed and installation of machinery is going on for mobiles, IT hardware products and automotive displays.

ledger.quote: The outlook for ‘25, ‘26 is very promising with healthy order book, and we are confident of achieving 50% growth this fiscal.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.verdict: Achieved 25.8% revenue growth in FY26 to Rs 48,873 crore against promised 50% growth.
ledger.evidence: Revenue FY25 Rs 38860.0 crore, FY26 Rs 48873.0 crore

ledger.quote: Our construction for capacity expansion for FATL in Tirupati will be ready by August ‘25 to meet the increased order book for our customers.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.verdict: FATL capacity expansion in Tirupati targeted for August 2025 was delayed to Q3 FY27.
ledger.evidence: Addition of our new manufacturing facility in Tirupati will expand our capacities from 0.6 million units per annum by another 0.3 million units per annum, including fully automatic front-loading washing machine 9, which will be launched in Q3 of this fiscal.

ledger.quote: We feel that this number of INR7,000-odd crores can ramp up to almost INR11,000, 12,000 crores.
ledger.speaker: Atul Lall
ledger.verdict: Targeting Rs 6,700-7,000 crore telecom revenue in FY27 towards ultimate scale up.
ledger.evidence: we feel, as I mentioned earlier, we're going to be somewhere between INR6,700 crores to INR7,000 crores in this fiscal.

ledger.quote: In FY 26-27, we think we can expand the margins. Even after taking into account the PLI margin, which is our share of PLI margin going away, we can expand the margin to almost 120, 130 bps in FY 26-27and which should even be higher in FY 27-28
ledger.speaker: Saurabh Gupta
ledger.verdict: Margin expansion promised for FY26-27 compressed; margin restoration deferred to FY27-28.

read: Management consistently expands scale and secures major OEM partnerships, but operational start dates regularly slip by one to two quarters across multiple projects. Additionally, long-term guidance on margin expansion and revenue growth can be overly optimistic, as seen in missed FY26 growth targets.
questions: Why do commercial production timelines across display, washing machines, and SSDs consistently slip by a quarter?
What specific measures will ensure operating margins recover after the compression caused by Mobile PLI 1 expiry?
bull: FY26 revenue reached Rs 48,873 crore with operating cash flows expanding to Rs 1,782 crore.
IT hardware campus in Chennai successfully expanded into laptops, desktops, AIOs, and high-end gaming laptops.
bear: FY26 revenue growth of 25.8% fell well short of management's 50% target.
Commercial launches for display JV, Tirupati FATL, SSDs, and Vivo JV all slipped to Q3-Q4 FY27.
